title: Cosimplicial frames compute localized mapping spaces
statement:
A model category here is a complete and cocomplete category with classes $C,F,W$ of cofibrations, fibrations and weak equivalences; $W$ satisfies two-out-of-three and is retract closed, and $(C,F\cap W)$ and $(C\cap W,F)$ are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system means factorization of every morphism and the two mutually characterized diagonal-lifting classes. Trivial means also in $W$. An object is cofibrant when its initial map is in $C$, and fibrant when its terminal map is in $F$. Write $q_{\mathcal M}:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M_\infty=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$ for homotopy coherent localization, universal for inverting $W$ including mapping spaces and composition homotopies. Infinity categories are modeled by simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with fillers for all inner horns (the union of all faces of a standard simplex except a face other than the first or last). All required universes may be enlarged.

For a cofibrant object $X$ of any such $\mathcal M$, a cosimplicial frame is a functor $X^\bullet:\Delta\to\mathcal M$ with $X^0=X$, an augmentation $X^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}X$ that is an objectwise weak equivalence and whose degree-zero component is the identity of $X$, and cofibrations $L_nX^\bullet\to X^n$ for all $n$. Here $\Delta$ has finite nonempty ordered sets and order-preserving maps, and $L_n$ is the colimit over nonidentity injective maps $[k]\hookrightarrow[n]$. Such frames exist. Every object of $\mathcal M_\infty$ is equivalent to the image of a cofibrant object and to the image of a fibrant object. For every fibrant $Y$, the simplicial set $H(X^\bullet,Y)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(X^n,Y)$ is Kan and represents $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qX,qY)$, naturally in the homotopy theory of both inputs. A Kan complex means a simplicial set in which every horn has a filler. Every component of this mapping space is represented by an actual map $X\to Y$. If $p:Y\to Z$ is a fibration between fibrant objects, $H(X^\bullet,p)$ is a Kan fibration, trivial if $p$ is trivial. A Kan fibration means a map with the right lifting property for every horn inclusion. A strict pullback of Kan complexes along a Kan fibration represents their homotopy pullback, and finite products of these Kan fibrations are Kan fibrations. If $T:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$ is the left adjoint of an adjunction and preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations, then $T$ preserves weak equivalences between cofibrant objects, $TX^\bullet$ is a frame on $TX$, and these mapping-space identifications are compatible with the functor induced by $T$ on cofibrant objects and by localization. In particular they identify evaluation and restriction maps whenever those are left Quillen functors. No simplicial enrichment, properness or combinatorial hypothesis is required.

source.place: Hovey Definition 5.2.7, Theorem 5.2.8, Corollary 5.4.4 and Proposition 5.4.7 (frames and Kan mapping complexes); Lemma 1.1.12 (Brown). Hinich, Dwyer-Kan localization revisited, arXiv:1311.4128v4, Proposition 1.2.1 and Theorem 1.3.3 (= Dwyer-Kan, Function complexes in homotopical algebra, 4.4), for identification with the universal infinity localization. Cisinski, Higher Categories and Homotopical Algebra, Corollary 3.8.4 and its proof, printed pp. 123-124, give the strict-pullback computation along a Kan fibration; finite products preserve Kan fibrations by componentwise horn lifting. No Stacks tag states the localization comparison.

external.place: Section 1.2 and Theorem 1.3.3, printed pp. 5-7; read online, including the displayed comparison with hammock localization.
Corollary 3.8.4 and proof, printed pp. 123-124; Corollary 3.1.28 and Theorem 3.1.29, printed p. 87.

proof.text: Factor $0\to V$ as $0\to QV\xrightarrow{\sim}V$ with $QV$ cofibrant and the last map a trivial fibration. Factor $V\to *$ as a trivial cofibration $V\xrightarrow{\sim}RV$ followed by a fibration. Since the localization inverts these maps, $qV\simeq qQV\simeq qRQV$ and $qV\simeq qRV$. This proves both assertions about object representatives, directly from the two factorization axioms. The functorial $Q$ preserves weak equivalences: for $w:V\to V'$ use $q_{V'}Qw=wq_V$ and two-out-of-three. On the full subcategory of cofibrant objects its restriction and the inclusion are inverse after localization, since the natural transformations $Q\to1$ have weak-equivalence components. This assertion uses the universal property including natural transformations, not just its set of objects.

source.place: Section 1.1 factorization axioms and Section 1.2 replacements

proof.text:
Give $\Delta$ degree $n$, with lowering maps the surjections and raising maps the injections; every order-preserving map factors uniquely through its ordered image. Put $(\ell X)^n=\coprod_{0\leq j\leq n}X$, with the evident fold map $\ell X\to\operatorname{const}X$. Use [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] to factor it into a Reedy cofibration $\ell X\to S^\bullet$ and a Reedy trivial fibration $S^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}X$, keeping the degree-zero factorization $X\xrightarrow{1}X\xrightarrow{1}X$. Explicitly, after degrees $<n$ have been constructed, factor
$$ (\ell X)^n\amalg_{L_n\ell X}L_nS\longrightarrow X\times_{M_n\operatorname{const}X}M_nS $$
into a cofibration followed by a trivial fibration; the degree-extension statement makes this a compatible functor and augmentation. For $n>0$, $L_n\ell X\to(\ell X)^n$ is an isomorphism, since each vertex factors through $[0]$ and the latching identifications identify its repeated occurrences. Thus the left source is $L_nS$. At $n=0$ the latching map is $0\to X$, a cofibration by the hypothesis on $X$. The objectwise assertion for Reedy trivial fibrations makes every $S^n\to X$ a trivial fibration. Hence $S$ is a frame as defined in the item, with the stronger augmentation property needed later. This construction is functorial. In the opposite model category it gives, for fibrant $Y$, a Reedy fibrant simplicial object $B_\bullet$ with $B_0=Y$ and $\operatorname{const}Y\to B_\bullet$ a Reedy trivial cofibration, hence objectwise a trivial cofibration. Indeed the right adjoint to degree-zero evaluation has degree $n$ the product of $n+1$ copies of $Y$, is Reedy fibrant, and the dual factorization ends in this diagram.

source.place: Theorem 5.2.8 and its fixed-degree-zero induction, printed pp. 127-128

proof.text: Let $A^\bullet$ be any frame on the cofibrant $X$, not necessarily the special one just constructed. Define $V_A(K)=\int^{[n]\in\Delta}K_n\cdot A^n$, where $K_n\cdot A^n$ denotes the coproduct of copies indexed by $K_n$. Concretely this is the coequalizer of $\coprod_{\theta:[m]\to[n]}K_n\cdot A^m\rightrightarrows\coprod_n K_n\cdot A^n$, using the simplicial operator on $K$ in one arrow and $A(\theta)$ in the other. Giving a map out of this coequalizer is exactly giving maps $K_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(A^n,Y)$ compatible with all operators. Hence $V_A\dashv H(A,-)$ and $V_A$ preserves colimits. The same formula gives $V_A(\Delta^n)=A^n$; for the boundary only the proper injective faces are needed, so $V_A(\partial\Delta^n)=L_nA$. The boundary criterion of [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] now shows that $V_A$ sends monomorphisms to cofibrations. The collapse to $\Delta^0$ is the augmentation $A^n\to X$, a weak equivalence by the frame hypothesis, so that criterion also makes every horn image a trivial cofibration.

A lifting problem for a horn inclusion against $H(A,p)$ is, by the adjunction of step 3, exactly a lifting problem for $V_A(\Lambda_i^n)\to A^n$ against $p$. Since that left map is a trivial cofibration, any fibration $p$ admits the required lift. If $p$ is a trivial fibration, the same argument for boundaries works because $L_nA\to A^n$ is a cofibration. The Kan-Quillen characterizations in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] identify the resulting maps as Kan fibrations and trivial Kan fibrations, respectively. Taking $p:Y\to *$ proves $H(A,Y)$ is Kan whenever $Y$ is fibrant. This proves the fibration clause even before restricting both endpoints to fibrant objects.

source.place: Corollary 5.4.4, with its adjoint lifting argument

proof.text: We will need invariance under weak equivalences rather than only trivial (co)fibrations. For a weak equivalence $f:Y\to Z$ of fibrant objects, use the fibrant factorization of [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]: $f=pi$ with $i:Y\to V$ a trivial cofibration, $p:V\to Z$ a fibration, and $r:V\to Y$ a fibration with $ri=1$. The object $V$ is fibrant, and two-out-of-three gives that $p,r$ are weak equivalences. Step 4 makes $H(A,p)$ and $H(A,r)$ weak equivalences. Since $H(A,r)H(A,i)=1$, two-out-of-three makes $H(A,i)$ a weak equivalence, hence so is $H(A,f)$. Apply steps 3-4 in $\mathcal M^{\mathrm{op}}$: if $B_\bullet$ is a simplicial frame on a fibrant $Y$, the contravariant $J(-)=\operatorname{Hom}(-,B_\bullet)$ sends trivial cofibrations to trivial Kan fibrations. For a weak equivalence $f:X\to X'$ of cofibrant objects, the cofibrant Brown factorization gives $f=pi$, $ps=1$ with $i,s$ cofibrations. Two-out-of-three makes both $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. Thus $J(i),J(s)$ are weak equivalences and $J(s)J(p)=1$ implies $J(p)$ is one too; consequently $J(f)$ is a weak equivalence. All intermediate cofibrant/fibrant conditions follow by composition of the specified cofibrations/fibrations.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12; the explicit Brown argument used in Proposition 5.4.7

proof.text:
For a frame $A$ and the simplicial frame $B$ of step 2, set $D_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}(A^m,B_n)$. Each $B_n$ is fibrant, all its structure maps are weak equivalences, and $Y\to B_n$ is one too. Step 5 says that the map from the constant simplicial diagram on $H(A,Y)$ to $n\mapsto H(A,B_n)$ is degreewise a weak homotopy equivalence. By [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence],
$$H(A,Y)\longrightarrow\operatorname{diag}D$$
is a weak homotopy equivalence. Every $A^m$ is cofibrant by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and all maps between degrees of $A$ are weak equivalences by the augmentation and two-out-of-three. The dual half of step 5 and the same diagonal theorem also give $\operatorname{Hom}(X,B_\bullet)\to\operatorname{diag}D$ as a weak homotopy equivalence. If $a:A\to A'$ is a map of frames whose degree-zero map is a weak equivalence, its components are weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. Applying the dual half of step 5 degree by degree to $\operatorname{Hom}(A'^m,B_\bullet)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A^m,B_\bullet)$ and then the diagonal theorem shows that the induced map on these diagonals is a weak equivalence. The square with the preceding $H(-,Y)$ comparisons and two-out-of-three therefore prove $H(A',Y)\to H(A,Y)$ a weak equivalence. This supplies the independence of frames used next.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.7 and Corollary 5.4.8; diagonal argument written for arbitrary frames

proof.text: The map $\ell X\to A$ induced by $A^0=X$ is a Reedy cofibration: in degree zero its relative latching map is $1_X$, and in every positive degree it is $L_nA\to A^n$. The lifting axiom in the Reedy model of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], against $S\to\operatorname{const}X$ from step 2, produces a map $A\to S$ over $X$, with degree-zero component $1_X$. All its components are weak equivalences by the two augmentations. Step 6 identifies $H(A,Y)$ with $H(S,Y)$ and then with $\operatorname{diag}\operatorname{Hom}(S^\bullet,B_\bullet)$. The special hypotheses are now verified: $S$ is Reedy cofibrant, $B$ Reedy fibrant, and their augmentation/coaugmentation maps are objectwise trivial fibration/trivial cofibration, respectively. None of these properties was silently assumed for the original arbitrary frame $A$.

Use [lem-coef-special-resolution-zigzag-nerve] for the special pair $(S,B)$. It compares the diagonal just obtained to the nerve of $\mathcal T(X,Y)$, whose objects are $X\xleftarrow{p}V\xrightarrow{h}W\xleftarrow{i}Y$ with $p$ a trivial fibration and $i$ a trivial cofibration. The intermediate comparison is the resolution-indexed diagram of the discrete sets $\operatorname{Hom}(S^m,B_n)$: the category $I(S,B)$ stated in the cited node (the two Grothendieck constructions) retains both chosen resolution indices and the map, and forgetting the indices gives precisely such a zigzag. This is why the special degreewise augmentation hypotheses in step 7, rather than merely objectwise weak equivalences, were required. Apply [lem-coef-special-hammock-reduction] to identify this nerve with $L^H(\mathcal M,W)(X,Y)$ by reduction of those diagrams to hammocks. Finally [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] identifies that hammock mapping object with the mapping space of the universal infinity localization. The composite is
$$H(A,Y)\simeq H(S,Y)\simeq\operatorname{diag}\operatorname{Hom}(S,B)\simeq N\mathcal T(X,Y)\simeq L^H(\mathcal M,W)(X,Y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M_\infty}(qX,qY).$$
These are equivalences of spaces, not an identification of sets of homotopy classes.

source.place: Propositions 3.5 and 3.7, realizing Dwyer-Kan 7.2; Hinich Proposition 1.2.1 for the last comparison

proof.text: Choose the special resolutions functorially by step 2. The comparison of [lem-coef-special-resolution-zigzag-nerve] is natural under maps of these resolutions; the endpoint actions on the special zigzags and their comparison with composition of hammocks are supplied by [lem-coef-special-hammock-reduction]. The comparison with the universal localization in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] respects its maps and composition homotopies. Thus step 8 is natural in the homotopy theory of both inputs. For other choices of $A$, the maps over $X$ in step 7 and the weak-equivalence invariance from step 6 give the same comparison in that homotopy theory. All normalization maps are identities in degree zero. In particular a vertex $f\in H(A,Y)_0=\operatorname{Hom}(X,Y)$ goes to the zigzag with identity outer arrows, hence to $q(f)$ by the last two cited statements. Every component of a simplicial set contains a vertex, so every component of the identified mapping space has an actual representative $X\to Y$.

source.place: Proposition 3.7(ii), Lemma 3.4 and normalization on vertices; Hinich Section 1.2

proof.text: Let $E\xrightarrow{p}C\xleftarrow{g}D$ be Kan complexes with $p$ a Kan fibration. Factor $g$ as a trivial cofibration $D\to D'$ followed by a Kan fibration $D'\to C$. The pullback of $D\to D'$ along the Kan fibration $E\times_C D'\to D'$ is a weak homotopy equivalence by right properness in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Its source is exactly $E\times_C D$. Its target $E\times_C D'$ is the homotopy pullback by the fibrant replacement description in that node. This proves the strict-pullback assertion without any properness assumption on $\mathcal M$. For a finite family of Kan fibrations, a horn lifting problem for the product is exactly the corresponding family of horn lifting problems; choose their fillers and take their product. For the empty family the product map is the identity on the terminal simplicial set, so the assertion includes that case.

source.place: Corollary 3.1.28; proof of Corollary 3.8.4, printed pp. 123-124

proof.text:
Let $T:\mathcal M\rightleftarrows\mathcal N:U$ be the indicated adjunction. Since $T$ preserves initial objects and cofibrations, it sends cofibrant objects to cofibrant objects. For a weak equivalence $f$ between cofibrant objects use [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to write $f=pi$, $ps=1$ with $i,s$ cofibrations. Both are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three, so $Ti,Ts$ are trivial cofibrations and $Tp\,Ts=1$ makes $Tp$ a weak equivalence. Hence $Tf$ is a weak equivalence. Every degree of a frame is cofibrant by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]; since $T$ preserves colimits,
$$L_n(TA)\cong T(L_nA),$$
and its latching maps are cofibrations. Its augmentations $TA^n\to TX$ are weak equivalences by the Brown argument, and its degree-zero augmentation is the identity. Thus $TA$ is a frame on $TX$. As in step 1, localizing the restriction of $T$ to cofibrant objects defines its derived functor on $\mathcal M_\infty$.

source.place: Lemma 1.1.12; Theorem 5.6.2, beginning of proof on preservation of frames

proof.text:
We verify compatibility on the actual weak-equivalence diagrams, without assuming that $T$ preserves trivial fibrations. First replace the fibrant target $Y$ by a trivial fibration $Y_c\to Y$ with $Y_c$ cofibrant. It is also fibrant; step 4 identifies the two source mapping complexes. Choose the special $S$ on $X$ and the special $B$ on $Y_c$ of step 2. Every $S^m$ and $B_n$ is cofibrant, the latter because $Y_c\to B_n$ is a trivial cofibration. Thus $T$ preserves all weak equivalences in their resolution diagrams by step 11. Let $r:TY_c\to Z$ be a trivial cofibration with $Z$ fibrant, and choose special resolutions $S'$ on $TX$ and $B'$ on $Z$ in $\mathcal N$. Reedy lifting from $\ell(TX)\to TS$ against the Reedy trivial fibration $S'\to\operatorname{const}(TX)$ gives $a:TS\to S'$ over $TX$, with $a^0=1$. All $a^m$ are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three. Since $T$ preserves colimits and (trivial) cofibrations, it preserves the relative latching formulas of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Thus $\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\to TB$ is a Reedy trivial cofibration. Lift this against $B'\to *$, starting from $\operatorname{const}(TY_c)\xrightarrow{r}\operatorname{const}Z\to B'$, to obtain $b:TB\to B'$ with $b_0=r$. Keeping this prescribed degree-zero lift uses the same degree-extension formula; all higher lifts have trivial-cofibration left maps and fibration right maps. Every $b_n$ is a weak equivalence, since $b_nT(i_n)=i'_nr$ and all the latter factors are weak equivalences.

Here is the comparison of mapping-space maps, with the contravariance in the first variable kept explicit. Write
$$D_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(S^m,B_n),\qquad E_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(TS^m,B'_n),\qquad D'_{m,n}=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal N}(S'^m,B'_n).$$
There are maps of bisimplicial sets
$$D\xrightarrow{\ h\mapsto b_nT(h)\ } E\xleftarrow{\ h'\mapsto h'a^m\ }D'.$$
All simplicial operators commute with these formulas by naturality of $a,b$ and functoriality of $T$. The second map is a weak equivalence on diagonals by the dual Brown invariance in step 5, since $a^m$ is a weak equivalence between cofibrant objects and $B'$ is a simplicial frame; apply [lem-coef-bisimplicial-diagonal-equivalence]. On frame complexes the maps are $H(S,Y_c)\to H(TS,Z)\leftarrow H(S',Z)$, respectively $h\mapsto rT(h)$ and precomposition with $a$. Their maps into the corresponding diagonals form commuting squares because $b_nT(i_n)=i'_nr$; all these vertical comparisons are equivalences by step 6. Thus this span gives the claimed simplicial map on mapping spaces.

It remains to check that this is the localization action. The general, hypothesis-free diagonal/index-category comparison explicitly stated in [lem-coef-special-resolution-zigzag-nerve] applies also to $E$ and to $\operatorname{Hom}(TS,TB)$; here no claim is made that the transported augmentation is a trivial fibration. For any of these pairs with weak-equivalence augmentations, forgetting the indices sends $(m,n,h)$ to its length-three zigzag in $L^H$; a string of arrows of $I$ is a commutative hammock, since its outer augmentation equations make its vertical arrows weak equivalences. This is a simplicial map by the face/degeneracy definition in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization]. Applying $T$ to the index-forgetting diagrams for $(S,B)$ is legitimate in the relative subcategory of cofibrant objects and gives $TX\leftarrow TS^m\to TB_n\leftarrow TY_c$. The maps $b_n$ compare this to $TX\leftarrow TS^m\to B'_n\leftarrow Z$, using $b_nT(i_n)=i'_nr$. The maps $a^m$ compare the latter diagrams for $h'a^m$ with $TX\leftarrow S'^m\xrightarrow{h'}B'_n\leftarrow Z$, using $p'^ma^m=T(p^m)$. In each comparison the indicated maps are vertical weak equivalences in commutative hammocks. Inserting these rows gives the simplicial homotopies; if the endpoint moves by $r$, use postcomposition by its length-one hammock, as in [lem-coef-special-hammock-reduction]. Consequently the span of diagonals above agrees with the literal action of $T$ on hammocks, followed by this endpoint replacement. Naturality of the general index comparison and of the localization comparison in [lem-coef-hammock-infinity-localization] identifies that action with the localized relative functor. Only the special pairs $(S,B)$ and $(S',B')$ use the special index-forgetting equivalence; no such equivalence is assumed for $(TS,TB)$ or $(TS,B') alone. Finally steps 6-7 transfer the conclusion from $S$ to any original frame $A$. These are comparisons of simplicial diagrams, not just a test on vertices. Inverting the source replacement $Y_c\to Y$ gives precisely the action of the derived functor defined on cofibrant objects in step 11. Taking $T$ to be an evaluation or restriction functor with the stipulated left Quillen adjunction proves the last clause. Only the stated model axioms have been used.

source.place: Low Lemma 1.4, Definition 1.5, Theorem 1.6, Lemma 3.4 and Proposition 3.7: mixed-variance Hom span, general index-category comparison and vertical hammock rows; comparison lifts use Hovey Theorem 5.2.5; localization functoriality uses Hinich Proposition 1.2.1. The latter sources are specified in the cited Reedy and hammock-localization nodes.
